query: SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE database_name='mvt' ORDER BY schema_name,function_name
rows: Decode vector tile BLOBs from a query (tile, z, x, y) into one row per feature

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Table in-out function: pass a subquery whose rows hold vector tiles and get one row per feature back. The input needs a `BLOB` column `tile` (or `tile_data`; gzip is detected) and whole-number columns `z`, `x`, `y` in the XYZ scheme (row 0 at the north). MBTiles rows are TMS: convert with `(1 << zoom_level) - 1 - tile_row AS y`. Named arguments `layer` and `coordinates` work as in `read_tiles`. Output columns: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (GEOMETRY), properties (JSON). Use `read_tiles` instead when the tileset is a file or URL.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## mvt_decode(data, layer := NULL, coordinates := 'wgs84')

Explode vector-tile blobs that are already in DuckDB into features. Input rows need `tile` (`BLOB`) and XYZ `z`, `x`, `y`. MBTiles rows are TMS: flip them with `(1 << zoom_level) - 1 - tile_row`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Decode MBTiles rows read with DuckDB's sqlite extension", "sql": "SELECT layer, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.mvt_decode((SELECT tile_data AS tile, zoom_level AS z, tile_column AS x, (1 << zoom_level) - 1 - tile_row AS y FROM sqlite_scan('test/fixtures/sample.mbtiles', 'tiles') WHERE zoom_level = 2)) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY n DESC"}]

Read the features of one Mapbox Vector Tile (.mvt/.pbf) at a given z/x/y

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a single Mapbox Vector Tile file or URL into rows, one per feature. A tile stores coordinates relative to its own corner, so you must pass its zoom `z`, column `x` and row `y` (XYZ scheme, row 0 at the north) to get real coordinates back. Named arguments: `layer` (one layer, plus a typed column per attribute inferred from the tile) and `coordinates` ('wgs84', 'web_mercator' or 'tile'). Columns match `read_tiles`: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry, properties.

Read the features of a PMTiles, MBTiles or XYZ vector tileset as rows with a GEOMETRY column

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a Mapbox Vector Tile tileset back into rows, one per feature. `source` is a PMTiles archive (local path or http(s) URL, read with range requests), a local MBTiles file, or a tile URL template with `{z}/{x}/{y}`. Named arguments: `zoom` (defaults to the tileset maxzoom), `layer` (read one layer and add a typed column per attribute), `west`/`south`/`east`/`north` (WGS84 bbox; all four or none; required for URL templates), `coordinates` ('wgs84' default, 'web_mercator' or 'tile') and `max_tiles` (default 10000; the call fails rather than read more). A constant `WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, <geometry>)` (or ST_Within/ST_Contains/...) also narrows the tiles read, so it can replace the bbox arguments. Columns: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (GEOMETRY), properties (JSON) and, with `layer`, one typed column per layer attribute. `tile_edges` ('merge' default, 'clip', 'raw') controls features that cross tile edges: 'merge' returns one row per feature, joining the per-tile pieces that share a feature_id (features without an id may come back as several non-overlapping pieces); 'raw' returns each tile's copy, buffer included. A feature extending past the tiles read is cut at their edge. Use `tileset_layers` first to discover layer and attribute names.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## read_tiles(source, zoom := maxzoom, layer := NULL, west/south/east/north := NULL, coordinates := 'wgs84', max_tiles := 10000, tile_edges := 'merge')

One row per vector-tile feature, with a `GEOMETRY` column and a JSON `properties` column. Sources: PMTiles (file or URL), MBTiles (file) or an `{z}/{x}/{y}` URL template.

Pass `layer` to also get each attribute of that layer as its own typed column. Features crossing tile edges come back once (`tile_edges := 'merge'`); use `'raw'` for each tile's stored copy.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Features per layer of the fixture tileset: one row each, joined across tile edges", "sql": "SELECT layer, geometry_type, count(*) AS features, round(sum(ST_Area(geometry)), 1) AS area FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/edges.pmtiles', zoom := 3) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL"}, {"description": "Tag each city with the region polygon that contains it (NULL when none): a spatial join of two layers", "sql": "SELECT c.name AS city, r.label AS region FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY city"}, {"description": "A spatial filter on the geometry also chooses which tiles are read", "sql": "SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(8, 44, 18, 54)) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer"}, {"description": "Road kinds in the Protomaps Florence sample, read over HTTP range requests", "sql": "SELECT properties->>'pmap:kind' AS kind, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protomaps/PMTiles/main/spec/v3/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles', zoom := 14) WHERE layer = 'roads' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC"}, {"description": "US ZIP code areas touching a Manhattan bbox, from a remote PMTiles archive", "sql": "SELECT DISTINCT ZCTA5CE10 AS zip FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://r2-public.protomaps.com/protomaps-sample-datasets/cb_2018_us_zcta510_500k.pmtiles', zoom := 7, layer := 'zcta', west := -74.02, south := 40.70, east := -73.93, north := 40.80) WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(-74.02, 40.70, -73.93, 40.80)) ORDER BY zip"}]

COPY ... TO format that encodes rows with a GEOMETRY column as a PMTiles vector tileset

rows.vgi.doc_llm: A COPY TO format, not a table function: use it as FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles' in a COPY ... TO statement whose destination is a local .pmtiles path. Each row is a feature. The `GEOMETRY` column must be WGS84 lon/lat (or EPSG:3857). A `VARCHAR` column named `layer` (or `layer_column`) names each row's layer, so one COPY can write several layers via UNION ALL; without it every row goes to `layer` (default: the file name). A column named `feature_id` (or `id_column`) becomes the feature id, and a column named `properties` holding JSON objects is expanded into attributes, so read_tiles output can be written back. Every other column becomes an attribute (`VARCHAR`, numbers, `BOOLEAN`; dates as ISO text; lists and structs as JSON text); NULLs are omitted. Options: minzoom/maxzoom (default 0/14); minzoom_column/maxzoom_column for per-feature zoom ranges; simplify and buffer (pixels of a 256-pixel tile); extent (4096); max_tile_bytes (500000: fails rather than dropping features); max_tiles; name, description, attribution. ORDER BY sets drawing order. COPY reports the number of rows written.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## COPY ... TO (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles')

Encode a query's rows as Mapbox Vector Tiles in a PMTiles archive. One row is one feature; a `layer` column puts rows in different layers of the same tiles, so a single COPY of a `UNION ALL` writes a whole multi-layer basemap.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Write two cities as a one-layer tileset (zoom 0 to 8)", "sql": "COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)"}, {"description": "Re-tile every layer of an existing tileset into a new archive", "sql": "COPY (SELECT layer, feature_id, properties, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles')) TO 'sample-copy.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 4, name 'sample copy')"}]
